name: Perform a surgical case from admission to recovery
summary: On the day of surgery the patient is registered and admitted to same-day surgery, seen by the anaesthesiologist and surgeon, taken to the operating room and operated on by a team of surgeon, anaesthesiologist and two nurses who run the mandatory three-phase surgical safety checklist. The patient recovers in the post-anaesthesia care unit and goes home the same day or to a ward bed. Day-of-surgery cancellations, late starts, waits for the room to be turned over, defective instrument trays and holds in recovery while waiting for a ward bed set how many cases a room completes in a day.

baseline.org_archetype: A three-site Ontario community hospital corporation with about 17 operating rooms, a same-day surgery unit and recovery room at each site, surgeons and anaesthesiologists with privileges paid by OHIP, and unionized perioperative nurses and attendants.
baseline.notes: The case mix is about 70% day surgery. Emergency cases arriving from sx-emergency-surgery follow the same steps from s04 with shorter waits; they are folded into the volume.

trigger: A booked patient arrives for surgery on the day on the final slate, or an add-on urgent case is called to the OR.
end_state: The patient leaves recovery for home or a ward bed, or the case is cancelled on the day.

volume.seasonality: Lower in July-August and late December (planned OR closures); very low in April-June 2020 and parts of 2021 (elective pauses); higher in February-March.

surge.cause: Fiscal year-end push to complete funded procedure volumes (February-March)

evidence.note: Author's estimate; quality-based procedure funding (src10) rewards completing volumes before March 31.
Volume from the organisation file (40,000-45,000 surgeries a year from the corporation's annual reports); not re-checked against those reports by this author.

steps.name: Register the patient at surgical admitting
steps.description: The patient arrives 1.5 to 2 hours before the scheduled time. The registration clerk confirms identity and health card, activates the pre-registered surgical visit in the hospital information system, prints the wristband and labels and sends the patient to same-day surgery.

error.defect_description: Wrong visit or wrong patient labels printed.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of community hospital practice; registration is in the organisation file's dh-patient-registration process but done at the surgical desk on the day.

steps.name: Admit the patient to same-day surgery
steps.description: The day surgery nurse checks the wristband, allergies, fasting, medications taken, escort home, consent and pre-admission results, takes vital signs, starts the IV and completes the pre-operative checklist in the chart.

error.defect_description: A missed allergy, medication or fasting problem is not recorded.

control.basis: Accreditation Canada required organizational practices: two patient identifiers and medication reconciliation at admission

next.condition: problem found: not fasting, results missing, consent unsigned, unwell or no escort

evidence.note: Patient readiness (missing blood work or investigations, unsigned consent) caused 23% of late starts in an Ontario hospital (wright2010) and patient and process factors drive day-of cancellations (leslie2013); minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Anaesthesiologist and surgeon decide to proceed or cancel
steps.description: The anaesthesiologist reviews the problem with the surgeon: a missing result may be done urgently, a patient who ate may be moved later in the list, while an unwell or unescorted patient is cancelled and returned to the booking office for a new date.

next.condition: case cancelled on the day of surgery

evidence.note: 8.07% of 19,141 elective cases at an Ontario teaching hospital (2005-2009) were cancelled on the day, 58.5% for process factors (leslie2013); urology at profile-matched Ontario hospitals ran 5.5%. The 4-5% cancelled here plus later cancellations give about 6%, the author's estimate for a community hospital.

steps.name: Anaesthesiologist assesses the patient in the holding area
steps.description: Between cases the anaesthesiologist reviews the pre-admission notes, examines the airway, confirms fasting and medications, explains the anaesthetic plan and obtains consent for anaesthesia or a regional block.

evidence.note: Anaesthesiologist availability was the largest single cause (24%) of late first-case starts (wright2010); minutes and waits are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Surgeon confirms consent and marks the site
steps.description: The surgeon sees the patient, confirms the procedure and side against the consent and booking, marks the operative site and answers last questions. Late lists may be cancelled here when an earlier case over-runs.

control.basis: Accreditation Canada and hospital policy: surgical site marking by the operating surgeon before the patient enters the OR

evidence.note: Surgeon availability caused 21% of late starts (wright2010); site marking is an Accreditation Canada practice; minutes and the over-run share are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Walk or wheel the patient to the operating room
steps.description: When the room is ready the OR attendant collects the patient from the holding area and takes them on a stretcher to the operating room, handing the chart to the circulating nurse.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the wait is for the room to be cleaned and set up after the previous case. Patient transport caused only 3.7% of late starts in wright2010.

steps.name: Set up the room and open the sterile trays
steps.description: The scrub and circulating nurses open the instrument trays and supplies from the case cart, check each tray's external and internal sterilization indicators and wrapper integrity, lay out instruments and do the first count.

control.basis: CSA Z314 and PIDAC best practice: check chemical indicators and package integrity before opening sterile items

next.condition: tray wet, torn, indicator failed or incomplete

evidence.note: Sterility indicators and package integrity are checked before use (pidac2013); minutes and defect share are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Replace a defective or incomplete tray
steps.description: The OR attendant fetches a backup set from sterile storage or medical device reprocessing; if none exists, reprocessing runs the set urgently and the case waits. The defect is reported to reprocessing.

control.basis: PIDAC best practice and CSA Z314: immediate-use steam sterilization not used for complete sets or implants

evidence.note: Immediate-use steam sterilization is for emergencies only and not for complete trays or implants (pidac2013); minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Run the briefing
steps.description: With the patient in the room, the circulating nurse as checklist coordinator leads the briefing with the surgeon and anaesthesiologist: identity, procedure, site, allergies, expected blood loss, antibiotic prophylaxis, equipment and implants.

control.basis: Ontario Ministry of Health mandatory three-phase surgical safety checklist (briefing, time out, debriefing) with public reporting of completion; Accreditation Canada required organizational practice

evidence.note: The checklist is complete only when the coordinator confirms all tasks in the briefing, time out and debriefing; Ontario completion was 98.4-99.3% in 2019-2022 (oh_ssc).

steps.name: Induce anaesthesia
steps.description: The anaesthesiologist applies monitors, gives the induction drugs or performs the spinal or block, secures the airway and positions the patient with the nurses.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; short for sedation and local cases, longer for regional blocks and difficult airways.

steps.name: Pause for the time out
steps.description: Before incision the whole team stops: the coordinator reads out patient, procedure, side and site, and the team confirms antibiotics given, imaging displayed and implants available.

control.basis: Ontario Ministry of Health mandatory three-phase surgical safety checklist (briefing, time out, debriefing) with public reporting of completion; Accreditation Canada required organizational practice

evidence.note: Time out is the second checklist phase (oh_ssc).

steps.name: Perform the operation
steps.description: The surgeon performs the procedure, from incision to closure, with the scrub nurse passing instruments; specimens are handed off for labelling.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for a community hospital mix of day surgery (cataracts, scopes, hernias, gynaecology) and inpatient cases (joints, bowel, hysterectomy).

steps.name: Scrub and circulate during the operation
steps.description: The scrub nurse passes instruments and keeps the count; the circulating nurse fetches supplies, labels specimens, documents implants and times, and runs the count at closure.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; runs for the length of the operation.

steps.name: Maintain anaesthesia during the operation
steps.description: The anaesthesiologist keeps the patient anaesthetized and stable, gives fluids, blood products and drugs, and records vital signs in the anaesthetic record.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; runs for the length of the operation.

steps.name: Do the final count and send specimens
steps.description: Before skin closure the scrub and circulating nurses count sponges, sharps and instruments against the record; specimens are bagged with the requisition and sent to pathology.

error.defect_description: A specimen is mislabelled or not sent.

control.basis: ORNAC perioperative standards and hospital surgical count policy (sponges, sharps, instruments)

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the count is an ORNAC standard and hospital policy.

steps.name: Resolve a count discrepancy
steps.description: The team searches the field, drapes and room; if the item is not found, an intraoperative X-ray is taken before the patient leaves, and an incident report is filed.

control.basis: ORNAC perioperative standards and hospital surgical count policy

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Wake the patient and run the debriefing
steps.description: The anaesthesiologist reverses the anaesthetic and extubates the patient while the coordinator runs the debriefing: procedure done, counts, specimens, equipment problems and concerns for recovery.

control.basis: Ontario Ministry of Health mandatory three-phase surgical safety checklist (briefing, time out, debriefing) with public reporting of completion; Accreditation Canada required organizational practice

evidence.note: Debriefing is the third checklist phase (oh_ssc); emergence times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Transfer to recovery and hand over
steps.description: The anaesthesiologist and circulating nurse wheel the patient to the post-anaesthesia care unit and give the recovery nurse a structured handover. If no recovery bay or nurse is free, the patient is held in the operating room.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; PACU holds are named in the organisation file's process description.

steps.name: Clean and turn over the room
steps.description: Two OR attendants remove waste, linen and the soiled case cart, wipe surfaces and equipment, mop the floor and bring in the next case cart.

control.basis: PIDAC environmental cleaning best practice and hospital OR cleaning procedure between cases

evidence.note: Author's estimate; turnover here is the time from one patient leaving the room to the room being ready for the next.

steps.name: Complete the intraoperative record and supply charges
steps.description: The circulating nurse finishes the intraoperative record in the OR module: times, staff, counts, implants with lot numbers, specimens and supplies used, which feed the supply reorder.

error.defect_description: Implant lot or supply missed in the record.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Write the operative note and post-operative orders
steps.description: The surgeon dictates or writes the operative note, writes post-operative orders and the discharge prescription for day patients, and talks to the family.

error.defect_description: Orders incomplete or unclear, so recovery nurses page the surgeon.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Recover the patient in the post-anaesthesia care unit
steps.description: The recovery nurse monitors airway, breathing, pain, nausea and the wound, gives medications and scores the patient against the discharge criteria before release.

control.basis: PACU discharge criteria (score-based) approved by the department of anaesthesia

evidence.note: Author's estimate; roughly 70% of community hospital surgery is day surgery.

steps.name: Recover in the day surgery unit and discharge home
steps.description: The day surgery nurse sits the patient up, gives fluids, checks pain and walking, reviews written discharge instructions and prescriptions with the patient and escort, and discharges them.

error.defect_description: Instructions not understood; patient phones or returns to the ED.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Request an inpatient bed
steps.description: The recovery nurse calls the patient flow coordinator for the bed booked on the slate; when no bed is clean, the coordinator finds one on another unit and the patient waits in recovery.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Porter takes the patient to the ward
steps.description: When the bed is ready a porter comes to recovery and wheels the patient on the stretcher to the surgical unit, where the recovery nurse's report has already been phoned through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the wait is for a clean bed and a porter, and holds recovery bays.

exceptions.name: Problem found at admission
exceptions.description: The patient is not fasting, results are missing, consent is unsigned, the patient is unwell or has no escort; about half are cancelled.

exceptions.name: Defective or incomplete instrument tray
exceptions.description: A tray is wet, torn, missing an instrument or has a failed indicator; a replacement is fetched while the room waits.

exceptions.name: Count discrepancy
exceptions.description: The final count does not match; the team searches and takes an X-ray before the patient leaves.

exceptions.name: Recovery hold waiting for a ward bed
exceptions.description: Inpatients wait in recovery for a clean bed and a porter, holding a recovery bay and sometimes the OR.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from arrival at surgical admitting to leaving recovery (about 5.5 and 8.5 hours)
benchmarks.population: Community hospital surgical cases, mixed day and inpatient

evidence.note: Author's estimate: arrival 1.5-2 hours before surgery, about 1-1.5 hours in the room for a typical community case, 1-2 hours in recovery and day-surgery discharge.

benchmarks.population: Kingston, Ontario, general surgery, gynaecology and urology, 2005-2009

evidence.note: 1,544 of 19,141 cases; process factors 58.5%.

benchmarks.unit: share of surgeries with all three phases completed
share of first cases in the room by 08:00

pain_points.description: Cases are cancelled on the day for problems that could have been caught earlier: missing results, unsigned consent, fasting errors, no escort or no bed.

evidence.note: 8.07% day-of-surgery cancellations, most for process factors.

pain_points.description: Late first-case starts while waiting for the anaesthesiologist, the surgeon or patient readiness lose room time every morning.

evidence.note: Cause shares 24%, 21% and 23% in wright2010.

pain_points.description: Room turnover between cases depends on two attendants and the next case cart; delays are common when attendants cover several rooms.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; named in the organisation file's description.

pain_points.description: Inpatients wait in recovery for a ward bed, which fills recovery bays and can stop the OR from sending the next patient.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; PACU holds are named in the organisation file's description.

pain_points.description: Wet, incomplete or wrongly assembled instrument trays hold the room while a replacement is found.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

assumptions: The simulated median (about 7.4 hours) is about 1.35 times the 5.5-hour estimate because the waits before surgery include cases later in the day that wait for earlier cases to finish; the estimate itself is the author's, not a measured figure. The case mix is a community hospital blend: skin-to-skin time 10-130 minutes (mode 35), about 70% day surgery. Endoscopy done in separate rooms is a separate process; if the organisation file's 3,700 surgeries a month include endoscopy and minor procedures, the long cases here overstate the average.

Work done together is split into parallel steps for each role (s12 surgeon, s13 two nurses, s14 anaesthesiologist; s19 to s22 room turnover, record, operative note and the start of recovery) linked with concurrent_with, so labour is counted per role and elapsed time once. Room turnover therefore runs while the patient is in recovery and does not lengthen the patient's cycle.
The briefing, time out and count are attributed to the circulating nurse as checklist coordinator; the surgeon's and anaesthesiologist's few minutes in them are not counted separately.

Operating room occupancy is counted from tray opening (s07) to the start of room cleaning, plus turnover; this is about 1.5 hours per case at the mode. Against the organisation file's 17 rooms at about 165 hours a month each (about 2,800 room-hours), 3,700 cases would need about 5,500 room-hours, so the organisation file's OR count or hours look low, or a large share of reported surgeries are short procedures outside the main ORs.
Surgical assistants (family physicians or second surgeons) who help in larger cases are not modelled.
Registration clerks, the bed flow coordinator and porters do steps in this process but are not in the organisation file's role list for it.

Hands-on time x volume implies about 230 FTE against about 265 stated. Stated nursing FTE is higher than hands-on time because perioperative nurses are scheduled for whole room days and stay with the room through turnover, late starts and gaps between cases. Anaesthesiologists' implied time (about 40 FTE at 130 hours) equals the organisation file's headcount of 40, which leaves little room for their obstetric, ICU and on-call work unless they work well over 130 hours a month, as physicians commonly do.

Organisation file corrected on 2026-11-24: operating room cases are the reported surgeries less endoscopies (about 1,300 a month, counted in sx-endoscopy and done in the endoscopy rooms), about 2,450 a month. Previously all 3,700 reported surgeries went through the operating rooms, which needed about twice the room hours the 17 rooms have. Stated FTE on this process were scaled to the new volume.
